notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. DBENCH AND SYMBASE ARE THE SAME PRODUCT AT TWO AGES, both by Lázár Zoltán. dbench-0.42's 24 keywords are symbase-0.94's first 24, in the same order, with the same ids -- `db sel`, `db use`, `db address`, `db close`, `db flen`, `db fieldno`, `db saved on`, `db saved off` and on. Neither should be ported without the other open. SymBase 0.92's readme records a keyword REMOVAL -- "REM: Date functions removed to a separate extension / No more needs date.library" -- which is exactly the shape that makes one build's tokens detokenise to nonsense under another, so the `renumbered` verdict may apply across the family and has not been checked. THE ARCHIVE'S BEST EVIDENCE IS NOT THE GUIDE: `Symbiose.AMOS`, 29,912 bytes, is a complete application written against this extension, and a program that uses a keyword settles what it does better than a paragraph describing it. `Tools/CreateDBF` is a companion, `OBUDAAT.DBF` a 62KB sample database in dBASE III format -- so the on-disc format is a documented one and the port would not have to guess it -- and four .abk banks carry the interface graphics.
